newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up on weather, physical prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up on weather, physical prices.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Tuesday on expectations of air conditioning demand in the U.S. Southwest and higher physical power prices driven by rumors of an Arizona generation unit outage, industry sources said.

"The weather is having a lot to do (with the rise), but the real-time market has spiked up on this outage talk, and that seems to have had a lot to do with it as well," said one Houston-based futures trader.
Sources said rumors of a generation unit outage at the Navajo coal-fired plant near Page, Ariz., were pushing short-term physical power prices higher.

However, a spokesman for Salt River Project (SRP), which operates the three 750 megawatt (MW) units at the Navajo plant, said Tuesday the units were operating at near half capacity due to low regional electricity demand.

Each unit was available for full load, but unit 1 was at 425 MW, while units 2 and 3 were each at 325 MW, the spokesman said. "We have had a bit of a reprieve from summer weather for the last week and a half or so," he said.
Palo Verde (PV) next-day physical peak power was said to be trading near $24.50-25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from a range of $21.50-22.50 on Monday for Tuesday delivery.
As of 1310 EDT, NYMEX July PV was up 91 cents at $30.20 after exchanges in a range of $29.30-30.25, while August was up 62 cents at the day's high of $31.60 following trade as low as $31.00 per MWh.

July California Oregon Border (COB) futures were up 52 cents at the day's high of $19.85 following a low of $19.00, while August was up 30 cents at the day's high of $22.70 after trade as low as $22.45 per MWh.
As of 1235 EDT, NYMEX said an estimated 213 COB and 343 PV contracts had traded.

Forecasts called for triple-digit temperatures in the interior part of the Southwest through next week with strong air-conditioning demand, while the Northwest was forecast to experience cooler-than-normal spring weather.
More coal-fired generation was expected to return to service from maintenance outages and repair shutdowns over the short term.
The 750 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired plant in Nevada was expected to be on line near 1600 PDT Tuesday following a Saturday shutdown for maintenance.
Startup of a 185 MW unit 1 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was delayed to early Wednesday due to a boiler tube leak.
Also, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was expected to resume output later this week.
Separately, sources said concern over reduced Northwest power supplies to southern California this summer was also putting some upward pressure on futures.
A Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is expected to introduce a proposal later this week to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system in early July.
The plan called for a summertime rating for the intertie at 6,900 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
In the meantime, Bonneville Power Administration said last week the summer transmission capacity on the intertie should be reduced to 6,300, down 900 MW from current levels.
As of 15:05 EDT, July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas was trading up 0.3 cents at $2.15 per million British thermal units.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
